segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For since the Law has a shadow of the good things to come and not the very form of the realities, it can never, by the same sacrifices that are offered continually year after year, make perfect those who draw near.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered, since the worshipers, cleansed once for all, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But in those sacrifices there is a reminder of sins year after year,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, when Christ comes into the world, he says:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you prepared for me;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: in whole burnt offerings and sin offerings you took no pleasure.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about me—to do your will, O God.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After saying above,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sin offerings you did not desire, nor did you take pleasure in them,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: though these are offered according to the Law,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he then says,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look, I have come to do your will.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He does away with the first in order to establish the second.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And by that will we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And every priest stands day after day performing his service and offering again and again the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But this one, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: waiting from then on until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For by one offering he has made perfect for all time those who are being made holy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws on their hearts, and on their minds I will write them,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he adds,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “and their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no more.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, brothers and sisters, since we have confidence to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: by the new and living way that he inaugurated for us through the curtain, that is, his flesh,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And let us give thought to one another, to stir up love and good works,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: not abandoning our gathering together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the day approaching.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if we deliberately go on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains any sacrifice for sins,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but a terrifying expectation of judgment and the fury of a fire about to consume the adversaries.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Anyone who has rejected the Law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: How much worse a punishment, do you think, will be deserved by the one who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, regarded as common the blood of the covenant by which he was made holy, and insulted the Spirit of grace?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For we know the one who said,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and again,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The Lord will judge his people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It is a terrifying thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But remember the earlier days, when, after you were enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: at times being made a public spectacle by insults and afflictions, and at times becoming partners with those who were treated that way.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For you suffered along with the prisoners, and you accepted the seizure of your possessions with joy, knowing that you yourselves have a better possession, and a lasting one.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So do not throw away your confidence, which carries a great reward.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For you need endurance, so that, having done the will of God, you may receive what was promised.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “in just a very little while, the one who is coming will come and will not delay;

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: but my righteous one will live by faith, and if he shrinks back, my soul takes no pleasure in him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls.

notes.note: The Greek verb means to bring someone to the intended goal or completed state, not to make morally flawless. In Hebrews it describes worshipers being fully fitted to come into God’s presence, something the yearly sacrifices could not achieve. The traditional “make perfect” is kept, in its older sense of “complete.”

notes.phrase: a body you prepared for me
notes.note: Verses 5–7 quote Psalm 40:6–8 in its ancient Greek version, which the author hears as the words of Christ; the Greek leaves the speaker unnamed, and “Christ” is supplied from the preceding sentence. Where the Hebrew text has “ears you have dug for me,” the Greek version cited here reads “a body you prepared for me,” and the argument in verse 10 depends on that wording.

The Greek verb is built on the ordinary word for “holy” and means to bring someone into the sphere of what belongs to God. Most translations use “sanctified,” which hides that link and now suggests to many readers a doctrine of gradual moral improvement. The meaning is not disputed; the choice is one of clarity.

The phrase can go with what precedes (“one sacrifice for sins for all time”) or with what follows (“sat down for all time at the right hand of God”). Either fits the contrast with priests who stand and offer repeatedly, and translations and commentators are divided. The rendering here leaves it with the sacrifice.

The Greek has no words corresponding to “he adds”; the sentence begun with “after saying” in verse 15 is left without an explicit continuation. Most translations supply one here, so that the promise to remember sins no more is the point being drawn out. Some instead take the continuation to begin at “says the Lord” in verse 16.

The Greek plural, literally “brothers,” was the normal way to address a mixed group of men and women as members of one family. “Brothers and sisters” gives a modern reader that sense. Many recent translations do the same, while others keep “brothers.”

The word originally meant freedom to speak one’s mind, and by this period also the assurance of someone who can come before a superior without fear or shame. “Confidence” conveys that better than the traditional “boldness,” which can suggest audacity. Many modern versions also have “confidence” here; the difference is one of English nuance, not of meaning.

notes.traditional: that is to say, his flesh
notes.note: The phrase most naturally explains “the curtain”: Christ’s flesh, given up in death, is what the way into the sanctuary passes through. Some interpreters attach it to “way” instead, meaning the way opened by his human life and death, to avoid picturing his flesh as a barrier. The Greek allows both, and the wording here follows the majority reading.

“The day” is shorthand for the day of the Lord, the time of God’s judgment and deliverance announced by the prophets, which the first Christians connected with Christ’s return. The original readers needed no further explanation.

The Greek word means “ordinary,” the opposite of what is set apart for God, and in Jewish usage it could carry the sense “ritually unclean.” To regard the covenant blood as common is to treat it as no different from any other blood. “Common” keeps the contrast with “made holy”; most translations have “unholy” or “profaned.”

Some later manuscripts read “my chains” instead of “the prisoners,” making the sentence refer to the author’s own imprisonment, and add “in heaven” after “possession.” The King James Version follows both readings. The shorter text translated here is generally judged to be the earlier one.

notes.phrase: the one who is coming will come
notes.note: Verses 37–38 quote Habakkuk 2:3–4 in its ancient Greek version, introduced by a phrase from Isaiah 26:20 (“a very little while”). The author reverses the order of the two clauses of Habakkuk 2:4, so that “shrinks back” is said of the righteous one, and understands “the one who is coming” as the returning Christ.

The Greek word covers both “faith” and “faithfulness,” and Habakkuk’s Hebrew speaks of the righteous person’s steadfastness; some manuscripts of the Greek version have “by my faithfulness,” meaning God’s. Hebrews places “my” with “righteous one,” though a few manuscripts differ, and goes on in the next chapter to describe faith as trust that holds firm. “Faith” is therefore used, with steadfast loyalty as part of what is meant.

candidates.reason: The plural address to mixed congregations recurs throughout the letters and Acts, and translators divide between “brothers” and “brothers and sisters,” so one policy is needed.
The word recurs in Paul, Hebrews and 1 Peter with a range from “awareness” to moral “conscience,” and the line between the two needs to be drawn once.
It recurs across the Gospels, Paul and Hebrews, and the choice between “covenant,” “testament” and “will” (especially Hebrews 9:16–17 and Galatians 3:15) must be coordinated.
Translations vary among “patience,” “endurance,” “perseverance” and “steadfastness” across Paul, Hebrews, James and Revelation, and readers should see one word.
The neuter plural for the sanctuary recurs through Hebrews 8–13 and is variously rendered “holy places,” “Most Holy Place,” “holiest” and “sanctuary”; the existing ἅγιος entry does not settle it.

warnings: Verse 19: ἅγιος is not rendered with a register form (holy ones; holy) and has no register-exception note.
Verse 29: ἁγιάζω is not rendered with a register form (make holy; consecrate; hold holy / honor as holy; be holy) and has no register-exception note.
